items.title: Anthropic Raises $107.3 Billion in Watershed AI Debut
items.summary: Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised a record $107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and private placement, making it the first frontier AI lab to tap public markets. Shares priced around a $1.5 trillion valuation and the stock jumped as much as 17% on its Nasdaq debut before volatility set in over the following days.
items.why_it_matters: It's the largest IPO ever and the first time a leading AI lab has gone public, turning Wall Street's bet on frontier AI into a real-time, tradable referendum.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
items.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge says he proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of the hardest open problems in mathematics, with help from Claude. The claim is still unverified, and TechCrunch notes a competing, non-AI proof attempt surfaced around the same time, so mathematicians are still working through both.
items.why_it_matters: If confirmed, it would be one of the biggest AI-assisted breakthroughs in pure mathematics yet, though the controversy around competing claims shows the result isn't settled.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of an affair, including allegations involving a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. The board's main concern, according to Wired, was his lack of candor, and the fallout has triggered an SEC accounting probe, a California attorney general subpoena, and a planned Senate hearing.
items.why_it_matters: Nvidia is the linchpin of the AI hardware industry, and the sudden loss of its longtime CEO amid a national-security-tinged scandal creates real uncertainty for the whole AI supply chain.

items.title: Wall Street Reels as AI Fears Erupt; Nasdaq 100 Near Bear Market
items.summary: A market-wide selloff hit Wall Street as concerns about the AI trade intensified: Anthropic slumped after its public debut, Nvidia sank 14%, and the Nasdaq 100 approached bear-market territory. The Nasdaq Composite went on to erase all of its 2026 gains as the selloff spread to emerging markets as well.
items.why_it_matters: Much of the stock market's gains this year have been tied to AI spending expectations, so a selloff of this scale signals investors are now questioning the pace and payoff of AI buildout.

items.title: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
items.summary: Lawmakers disclosed that the Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, some with military ties, intensifying calls in Congress to tighten export controls in the wake of the Jensen Huang scandal. Reporting ties the disclosure to broader concern that China's AI firms, long dependent on Nvidia chips, now face a supply withdrawal.
items.why_it_matters: Chip export policy directly shapes who gets access to the compute that trains frontier AI, and this disclosure adds fuel to a fight in Washington over China access.

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.summary: OpenAI described a layered defense against adversarial distillation, combining model training, safeguards, detection and enforcement to stop outside parties from extracting its models' capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: Distillation attacks let competitors cheaply copy a frontier model's capabilities, so defenses against it protect the economics of training expensive frontier models.

items.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
items.summary: A now-removed Apple job listing shows the company is hiring an engineer to lead creation of an agentic AI system that can browse the web, work across apps, write code and call services on a user's behalf, putting Apple in direct competition with Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic's agents.
items.why_it_matters: Apple has lagged in generative AI, so a dedicated push to build its own autonomous agent would be a significant competitive shift.

items.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.summary: A researcher seeded 2 million unique, trackable "canary" secrets into prompts across the AI supply chain and found that the data doesn't stay private, surfacing widespread leakage.
items.why_it_matters: The experiment gives concrete, large-scale evidence that user data fed into AI systems can leak further than users expect, a core trust issue for the industry.

items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: A new paper describes language models that can rewrite their own weights, drawing heavy discussion on Hacker News (343 points, 112 comments).
items.why_it_matters: Self-modifying models raise major questions for AI capability growth and control if models can alter themselves rather than only being trained externally.

items.title: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI
items.summary: A blog post describes "Frostbite," a new CPU architecture reportedly discovered, designed and verified by AI, which drew strong engagement on Hacker News (548 points, 292 comments).
items.why_it_matters: An AI system independently producing a verified hardware architecture would be a notable step beyond AI assisting human chip designers.
